fields.meta_title: Team Registration Form for Captains and Players | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a team registration form: the captain registers once, each player joins by link, and the roster saves to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Team Registration Form Captains Start and Players Finish
fields.hero_description: Build a team registration form where the captain signs up the team and each player joins and signs from their own link.
fields.features_heading: What a League Needs From Every Team
fields.features_subheading: A team registration form has two authors. The captain starts the entry, and every player fills in the details only they know.
fields.feature_1:
Teammates invited by email

The captain enters the team name and each teammate's email address. Every player then gets a link to fill in their own details, and the captain never has to type them in.
fields.feature_2:
Roster minimums and caps

The form counts players as they join. Set the number that confirms a team and the number that closes its roster, and the captain sees how many of the spots are still open.
fields.feature_3:
Team names checked against the league

A name that another team already holds is refused, and the captain is asked for a new one before anything saves. Each name on the schedule then points to exactly one team.
fields.feature_4:
A waiver signed from each player's link

Each player signs the league waiver from their own link, and the app captures the signature and the date. The roster shows who has signed and who has not signed yet.
fields.feature_5:
Late roster swaps sent for approval

Set a date when rosters lock. After it, a captain's swap waits in a queue, and the organizer gets an email or a Slack message asking them to approve it or turn it down.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to move

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Run registration on your own servers, next to the league website and the game schedule you keep there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Leagues That Register by the Team
fields.tab_content_1:
Late Kickers fills its 12th spot with Haruto

Thistlewood Social Club confirms a kickball team at 12 players. Captain Benedetta Ingersoll enters the emails of 11 teammates. Each opens a link, adds a name, phone number, and shirt size, and signs the waiver. Haruto Becerra signs as player 12, and Benedetta gets an email that Late Kickers is confirmed.
fields.tab_content_2:
No fifth seat on a hackathon team of 4

Pembrook Hack Weekend takes teams of 2 to 4. Team lead Cosima Thibodeaux registers Null Island in the Climate track and adds 3 teammates by name and email. With 4 members listed, the form stops offering another slot. Organizer Inez Pilkington sees Null Island on the Climate track list with its 4 members.
fields.tab_content_3:
One league, no two teams with the same name

The Gilded Anchor runs a Wednesday trivia league where every team name is different. Captain Ondine Gaskell types The Know-It-Owls, but that team already plays on Wednesdays, so she is asked to pick again. She registers Second Guessers with 5 players. Tables seat 6, so the roster stops at 6 names.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every swap after the lock goes to Margit

Saltwick Lake rosters lock on August 1, at 20 paddlers and 1 drummer a boat. On August 4, Brightmoor Freight captain Anselmo Hakala swaps Dorian Saltz out for Priscilla Mbatha. The swap waits, and race director Margit Okwuosa gets an email asking her to approve it. Until she does, Dorian stays on the roster.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Team Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a team registration form that collects every player on the roster, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the smallest and largest roster
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the waiver at the end
fields.howto_step_1_des: Split the form into what the captain answers and what each player answers. The captain gives the team name and the teammates' emails. Players add their own contact details. Nobody has to guess a teammate's phone number or spell a name.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the smallest and largest roster your game allows. The smaller number confirms a team and the larger one closes its roster. Leave room for substitutes in the larger number, because a team that loses two players midseason still has to field a side.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask each player for only what the season needs: how to reach them, plus anything the league prints, such as a shirt size. Every extra question gives the last teammate one more reason to leave the link unopened until the deadline has passed.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place the league waiver at the end of each player's link, after the details the signature covers. Have your league's lawyer or insurer write the wording. The form collects the signature and the date the player signed.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the two parts, the roster limits, and the waiver into one prompt. Emergent builds the team registration form, the database behind it, and a page where organizers see every team. Change any part later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose who gets an email at each point: the captain when the team is confirmed, and an organizer when a swap arrives after rosters lock. Set the lock date now, before the first captain registers, and show it on the form where captains will see it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Register a test team with friends
fields.howto_step_7_des: Register a fake team with three friends before the link goes out. Check that each friend's link opens their own page, that the player count rises as each one signs, and that the confirmation email reaches the captain's inbox.

faq_plan.q: What is a team registration form?
faq_plan.a: A team registration form signs up a whole team in one entry instead of one person at a time. A captain or coach gives the team's name and contact details and lists the players. Each player's details and signature then attach to that team's record, which is how a league or club builds its rosters before a season.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a team registration form?
faq_plan.a: Decide what the captain fills in, what each player fills in, and how many players make a team. Describe all three in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form, the player links, and a database that holds every roster you collect.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a team registration form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with two groups of fields. For the team: its name, the captain's name, email, and phone, and a division if you run more than one. For each player: a name, a phone number, and a waiver signature. Add a shirt size only if the league prints shirts.

faq_plan.q: Can players fill in their own details on a team registration form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The captain enters each teammate's email, and every player gets a link to add their own name, contact details, and signature. A team registration form PDF cannot split that way, because one person fills in every line. For youth baseball, where a parent registers each child, a little league registration form fits better than a captain's form.

faq_plan.q: How many players should a team registration form allow on one roster?
faq_plan.a: Set it from your game's own rules: the players a side needs on the field, plus room for absences. Put a minimum on the form to confirm a team and a maximum to close its roster. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, and a league with 80 teams registers every one of them.

faq_plan.q: How do I get every player to sign the waiver on a team registration form?
faq_plan.a: Place the signature last in each player's link, and count a player on the roster only once they sign. The app captures each signature with its date, and the captain sees who has not signed yet. Take the waiver wording from your league's counsel. The form only collects the signatures.

faq_plan.q: How is a team registration form different from a one-person sign-up?
faq_plan.a: A team registration has two layers: the team, entered once by a captain, and the players, each tied to that team. A one-person sign-up, like a summer camp registration form, stops at one participant and a guardian. The team layer is what lets a league confirm, cap, and schedule whole teams.

faq_plan.q: How does a team registration form stop duplicate team names?
faq_plan.a: Check each new name against the names already registered, and refuse a match before the form saves. Ask the captain for another name on the same screen. Compare names without case or extra spaces, because Night Owls and night owls are one team on a schedule. Emergent builds the team table into a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a captain change the roster after sending a team registration form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, until a lock date you choose. Before it, a captain swaps players freely and the new player gets their own link. After it, a swap waits for an organizer to approve it, and the old player stays on the roster until then. Print the lock date on the form where captains see it before they register.

faq_plan.q: Can one team registration form handle several divisions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask the captain to pick a division first, and give each division its own roster size and its own cap on teams. A coed division and an open one can then fill at different rates. Divisions work like sections on a class registration form, each with its own count of open places.

The page wins on that two-layer flow (captain fields, player links, roster minimums and caps, unique team names, roster locks) across four adult team settings that the youth, tournament and Little League siblings do not cover.
